name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 18 points, anchoring a large expected margin
Incumbent George Latimer has a clear fundraising edge; challenger Joseph Cinquemani shows no reported money
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Latimer's incumbency and roughly half-million-dollar war chest, and a challenger with no visible fundraising all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at about 98 percent for Democrats. With no contrary evidence in polls, ratings, or spending, there is no basis to move off a Safe Democratic assessment.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Latimer or unusually low turnout in this low-salience race could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-16 is a heavily Democratic district in Westchester County, with a partisan lean of roughly 18 points toward Democrats. George Latimer, a first-term incumbent who won the seat in 2024, is running for reelection and holds a clear financial advantage, having raised about half a million dollars. Republican Joseph Cinquemani shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand, leaving him little visible infrastructure for a general-election campaign.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent. The combination of a strong Democratic lean, an established incumbent, and an underfunded challenger makes this seat solidly Democratic heading into November, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than competitiveness.
